verdict.tagline: Epic sci-fi journeys built on legendary characters and dated mechanics.
for_you_if: you want to experience a sweeping space opera trilogy
you can appreciate classic storytelling despite mechanical age
you enjoy deep character progression across multiple games
not_for_you_if: you will not install a third-party application to play
you need modern combat mechanics in the first installment
you require seamless offline play without account links

claims.claim: Reviewers experience technical issues where the game fails to launch or start.

citations.review_text:
No.
This game won't start.

This game does not launch with Proton (on Bazzite) because of the EA app.

Update: The game does not launch on Bazzite-deck stable version 43.20260420, the latest stable release as of writing this review. I tried several Proton versions, enabling IPv6 on the main ethernet configuration (Bazzite disabled it by default?) to resolve a known EA App networking bug, and attempted launching both in gaming mode and desktop mode, but every time the game fails to launch. 

On plain Fedora 44, the game launches fine with stock Proton using either GNOME Wayland or Gamescope.

claims.claim: Reviewers encounter startup failures or conflicts tied to the EA app integration.

citations.review_text: I love Mass Effect but do not recommend to buy this crap. Because of EA App theres so much conflicts and you can't just hit the button and start to play. Game in Steam Big Picture overlay is broken, window doesn't focus where it should, controller doesn't work as native as it should. If it works like ♥♥♥♥ i would recommend to just download it from fitgirl and dont give a penny to this broken company.

The Mass Effect trilogy is my favorite video game series of all time. I've played through both the originals and the Legendary Edition (on console) countless times, I know the deep bits of the lore, and I put hundreds of hours into the ME3 multiplayer (which is sadly missing from Legendary Edition, but that's not the problem). 

Due to the EA app integration, the Steam version of Mass Effect Legendary Edition is near-unplayable. Whenever I try to launch the game, unless I've freshly started or restarted my PC, it does not launch. When I press play after restarting my computer, it DOES start, but it doesn't bring up the launcher, only bringing me in to Mass Effect 1. It simply does. not. work.

Thanks EA, I'm disappointed. Refunding.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering bugs and crashes in the first game that require reloading previous saves to progress.

citations.review_text: I love these games but so far ME1 is riddled with bugs. I would have expected bugs from the main story to be fixed at the very least but playing on insanity I've had to go back to saves and replay several times because something got stuck or didn't load. The game seems to fix itself if I load a save far enough back but losing all that progress is really annoying. The game is more of a texture upgrade than it is a remaster so keep that in mind. idk if its worth the 60 bones especially if you already have the originals.
Very buggy, constant crashes in ME1. Disabled overlay, verified files. Constant saving needed to progress

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the first game as feeling dated in its animations, simple enemy design, and mechanical elements.

citations.review_text: Bought this on sale. Playing it for the first time as an adult gamer. Finished ME1 and now just started ME2. As I beat the games I will come back here and update my review of the overall franchise. ME1 was a solid 8/10 for me. Game is def dated and shows its age a bit with the animation and simple enemy design. Your here for the worldbuilding and story and side characters though, all of which are amazing. I played on normal difficulty and it was pretty easy, especially on mouse and keyboard, I was basically 2 tapping most of the basic geth near the end with my sniper. The open world parts in the rover were kinda boring too since 95% of the planet were barren and i ultimately abandoned them and just focused on the main story because it felt pointless. Looking forward to ME2 next! Took me 18 hours to beat ME1.

Nearly 20 years ago I started playing the original ME and was taken on an amazing journey that I have not forgotten. Loading back up brought back instant nostalgia of being younger and enjoying this game for the first time. So far the game looks as amazing as it did back then even though its been magnificently upgraded since then. Some of the mechanics do show their age but they are still very enjoyable. If you're a fan of sci fi such as the expanse, star trek, etc you will enjoy this game very much.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that side exploration in the rover feels repetitive due to barren planets.

citations.review_text:
Legendary Edition, mass effect 1, 2 and 3 included, with DLC.
I used to love these games when i had a ps3 many years ago.
Saw the legendary edition for sale and immediately bought it, great value for 3 games + extra content.
It runs great on my laptop which is a bit old, and a little outdated so was pleasantly surprised that it ran with no issues, on high settings. No lagging issues, even when in a busy environment, plays smooth, in fact better than the ps3 versions. 
I found it a bit different using the keyboard and mouse, so bought a controller if i choose to use it instead.

*Skip down if your not interested in hearing about the game.
A bit about the game, If your new to Mass effect, its a story driven game, so it can be a bit slow for some, but you can speed it up if your not into the story and just want action. There are a lot of things to do in the game! huge REPLAY value, Exploring the universe and planets, side missions, adjusting loadouts, character traits, great Visuals of new planets and colonies, interesting characters you meet, the choices you make in the story effects lots of things, including the members of the crew of your ship. The gameplay is great, amazing expansive visuals, Space/planets etc with your typical 3rd person action gameplay. You also can use powers or special abilities depending on the class you choose which in a firefight can be the difference between winning and losing. Things like teleport, pull, push, drone, incendiary ammo to name a few. 
When you get your ship, you can explore different systems and planets, find side missions, find new equipment, and harvest resources, get credits, to upgrade your ship, yourself or teamates. When starting a mission your able to choose two teammates, which also have unique albilities, to join you. Your teammates are also customisable, can change weapon loadouts, and can upgrade them and their abilities.
I got sick of popular fps games when i used to play on my ps3 many years ago, and i was more i…

Bought this on sale. Playing it for the first time as an adult gamer. Finished ME1 and now just started ME2. As I beat the games I will come back here and update my review of the overall franchise. ME1 was a solid 8/10 for me. Game is def dated and shows its age a bit with the animation and simple enemy design. Your here for the worldbuilding and story and side characters though, all of which are amazing. I played on normal difficulty and it was pretty easy, especially on mouse and keyboard, I was basically 2 tapping most of the basic geth near the end with my sniper. The open world parts in the rover were kinda boring too since 95% of the planet were barren and i ultimately abandoned them and just focused on the main story because it felt pointless. Looking forward to ME2 next! Took me 18 hours to beat ME1.

claims.claim: The game requires a third-party EA account and launcher to play, which can block access or break offline play.

citations.review_text: Don't bother purchasing this on Steam. EA will randomly "update" their launcher so you won't even be able to play the game. God forbid you play a single player game offline.

Great games but being forced to make an EA account to play single player games is heinous.

Mass Effect 1 is archaic and you can still see a lot of the DNA from KOTOR, but it's still a fun adventure. The gameplay is a bad covershooter and the AI is braindead, often getting stuck on geometry or running in circles. I still had a lot of fun flinging enemies around with the biotic powers though. The hacking minigame is overused and I started using the onmi-gel skip and then just skipping loot entirely in the end game because I was tired of it. The Mako driving sections were a lot more fun than I remember, maybe they improved the controls for the Legendary Edition. There was an annoying bug where Shepard(you) gets stuck facing right for a minute, changing the movement controls as well. It goes away after a little time but is still irritating. Overall, Biowares grasp exceeded it's reach as many parts of the game feel janky and barely held together, but the ambition and heart in this game in undeniable. The story, characters, and music are all great.

Loved the game. I have 25 hours in ME1 but now can not continue the game. The requirement for an account in the EA app for a single player game enrages me to no end. There was a workaround to skip the EA launcher but it stopped working. 
I WILL NEVER BUY AN EA GAME EVER AGAIN!

Still the point stands that an external launcher with online-only DRM shouldn't be required for a single-player title. Just be aware you can purchase this game and loose access to it at any time.

claims.claim: The combat mechanics and gameplay in the first installment feel dated and clunky compared to modern shooters.

citations.review_text:
This game is by far the best Sci-Fi RPG out there. Every entry in the series is an undeniable classic, and I cannot recommend this game more. The story is 10/10, every choice you make impacts the entire trilogy, and the lore is unbeatable. There are some minor issues that I need to point out however: The combat mechanics are very outdated, especially in Mass Effect 1 and 2. If you are a player used to modern AAA shooters, I would keep this in mind before you buy. On a more positive note, the controls are very easy and consistent with modern shooters, however if you are thinking of using a controller, I would use mouse and keyboard, as I find the quality of life on the latter device easier than on a controller, and hacking mini-games differ if you are using controller or keyboard, and I find the keyboard variant much more enjoyable (the controller/gamepad one being simply pressing the buttons prompted on screen). 

TD;LR: If you are a lover of Story-based RPGs, or if you just love Sci-Fi in general, there is not a single game I can recommend more.

Great games but being forced to make an EA account to play single player games is heinous.

Mass Effect 1 is archaic and you can still see a lot of the DNA from KOTOR, but it's still a fun adventure. The gameplay is a bad covershooter and the AI is braindead, often getting stuck on geometry or running in circles. I still had a lot of fun flinging enemies around with the biotic powers though. The hacking minigame is overused and I started using the onmi-gel skip and then just skipping loot entirely in the end game because I was tired of it. The Mako driving sections were a lot more fun than I remember, maybe they improved the controls for the Legendary Edition. There was an annoying bug where Shepard(you) gets stuck facing right for a minute, changing the movement controls as well. It goes away after a little time but is still irritating. Overall, Biowares grasp exceeded it's reach as many parts of the game feel janky and barely held together, but the ambition and heart in this game in undeniable. The story, characters, and music are all great.

One of the best sci-fi premises of all time, well executed. The gameplay in ME1 has aged a bit and feels a bit clunky compared to modern games, but it holds up surprisingly well. That aside the fantastic story and revolutionary (at the time) conversation mechanic carry the game through most if not all technical hiccups

Mass effect Legendary edition
	Gotta speedrun reviews, since this is a 3 for 1 package.
	
	ME1: A fun, but overall clunky experience. The shooting is a relic by modern standards and has no real challenge, and I think that is fair considering it is now 20 years old. The plot is simple, but the story really shines through because of the setting and fostering an inquisitive air about it. Similar to Metaphor: Refantazio, but in space. 
	
	ME2: Holy hell, this game is immediately better than 1, the RPG mechanics have been heavily simplified, the shooting feels much better, and the setting is even further expanded. The graphics are heavily improved, so much so that I feel worse about ME1 as a result. ME1 feels noticeably "sterile" while ME2 feels "lived in", the world certainly feels like the other space races have been here far longer than the humans have.
	
	ME3: havent gotten to it yet, i will return once i get through it to update my review.

claims.claim: This cohort mentions encountering technical glitches, softlocks during Ilos, and dated jank in the first game of the trilogy.

citations.review_text:
Aside from frustrations with ME1's jenkiness (which lead to many MANY frustrations with glitches and softlocks on Ilos), I have never loved a videogame series quite like Mass Effect. It has many, many flaws, but in the grand scheme of the characters, writing and storytelling, it pales in comparison. I'm not trying to make this all poetic but I'm being sincere, I'm writing this review after finishing ME3 for the first time.
I played this entire playthrough modded, qol stuff and textures to bring it to life - aside from plot hole fixes and the big one, an alternative ending to ME3 that places one of the DLCs at the end of the game as a post-credit farewell. I started with binging ME1 nonstop for a day and a half, then ME2 for about four days. Once I hit ME3 I started losing steam and took breaks to play other games between, but I've never devoured a game series in this manner before. Never have I sat looking at the menu screen when it was all over and felt a heartbreak in uninstalling the game - backing up EVERYTHING for an excuse to play new game + in the future. And for the first time, I KNOW  I will be coming back for a new game + version, something I've never felt the need or want to do in a story-driven videogame before. I have a hard time picking other options when I replay games, but I can say 100% without a doubt that this game has some insane replayability. This is one of the games I felt like I was there with the characters, and I felt like my Shepard was truly, 100% canon, when I know EVERY Shepard is canon. I can understand why this series is so beloved, even today. And despite being an EA product, despite the flaws and Ilos softlocks that made me want to throw my PC out the window, I wholeheartedly recommend Mass Effect to ANYONE who wants a good sci-fi story-driven game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the PC version has dual-monitor and resolution boundary issues that require manual .ini configuration file edits to resolve.

citations.review_text:
If you played before, you know exactly why, if you not played the trilogy yet, I am so envy of you because the first playthough will be amazing, secondly beg you to give the game a chance because worth it.

The Pc port is solid however have some issues, some minor texture bug, nothing gamebreaking, but the game not handle very well the dual monitor setups, the borderless Window and the 4k resolutions, Have an easy fix, you need modify the 
...\Steam\steamapps\common\Mass Effect Legendary Edition\Game\ME1\BioGame\Config\GamerSettings.ini

file and these lines.
BorderlessWindow=True
ResX=3840
ResY=2160

This fix working on all three game, I don't understand why not patched the devs this already... of course make a backup file before you do anything.

played Andromeda, couldn't get into it. This was on sale, it is my wifes favorite game, figured id give it a shot but didn't expect to like it. 124 hours and i finally got 100% achievements and beet all three games (with a tiny bit of help, my wife watching and telling me when i'm about to miss something important or miss an achievement and correcting it) I was drawn in, first game was just so good i couldn't put it down. There where a few hiccups especially playing on insanity for my first playthrough of all three games, and theres a bug in the second one where you dont get ammo drops so you have to beat entire sections and kill 100s of enemies with limited ammo eventually to a point where for large portions of the game youre just behind cover instructing teamates and waiting for it to be over. added a lot of extra time to the playthrough from that which i didnt know was a bug i just thought it was crappy level design. There where a few points that almost got a tear to fall out my eye which i didnt expect. You have to romance tali in both 2 and 3 but cant romance her in 1, you can romance liara in 2 but it doesnt give paramour achievement so its impossible to get paramour and stay loyal across all 3 games. a little crummy but with some save scumming and careful planning around that achievement i was able to get it. combat was improved with each game, glad the mako was gone in two but they solved the problem with the mako by giving us a flying/jumping hover craft and took away the planet exploration then removed it completely in 3 instead of giving the best of both worlds but honestly not that mad about it. The story is also extremely engaging, the amount of choices that you make and they way they affect future games, choices in 1 actually have a large impact in 3 and the outcomes of 3 either helping or hindering you and the impact of those choices are felt across the franchise and that is something that many franchises have tried but this is the only one that ive s…

citations.review_text:
the game itself is great.  have played the entire trilogy several times. what isn't great is that the app you you are forced to use has rendered the game completely unplayable. your controller will fail because steam / EA app overlays constantly cause interference. disabling them does not fix the problem. I know there is a MOD for this, but I'm not paying for a game that needs a mod to play and neither should you. 
Will never purchase from EA again - hope they go out of business. 
Steam needs to stop allowing this third party app ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

This is one of the best deals in gaming. These 3 games are literally Legendary. I replayed these games, in order after not playing them since the 3rd one came out. I had forgot a lot of what happens in 2 & 3. I played 80% of these games on the Steam Deck. They played wonderfully on default settings, 60 fps the whole way during heavy fighting, populated areas, etc. played so good. The only problem with this game on Steam Deck, which is a problem for all EA games on SD, the launcher. Im order to play this or any EA game, you have to download EA games launcher in desktop mode, add it as a non steam game,  get it set up and go back to gaming mode. When you launch the game, it will then work. This works with Titanfall 2, Battlefront 2, etc. Jmping through hoops to get thru the launcher really sucks and shame on EA but don't let that stop you from one of the greatest trilogies of all time.
